Headteacher’s Welcome
Dr Olivia Kurzeja – Headteacher
Welcome to Step by Step School.
We are an independent day school for autistic pupils, providing specialised teaching for Primary, Secondary and Sixth Form learners aged 4 to 19. Based just outside East Grinstead, Step by Step was founded in 2004 by a group of parents who had been running home‑based education programmes. Their vision was to create a school offering a highly specialised approach that met each pupil’s individual and autism‑specific needs within a social, community‑focused environment. That founding vision continues to guide us today and we proudly serve a wide area across the South East welcoming pupils from West Sussex and Brighton & Hove, to as far as Bromley, Croydon and Greenwich.
At Step by Step, we take great pride in creating a calm, nurturing space where pupils feel safe to explore, learn, and express themselves. Our dedicated staff are deeply committed to understanding each child as an individual, their strengths, their needs, and the unique ways they experience the world. This personalised approach sits at the heart of everything we do.
The defining aspect of our provision is the individualised programme each pupil receives throughout the school day. Behaviour analytic principles, Speech and Language Therapy, Occupational Therapy, Total Communication Approach, Attention Autism and the use of a range of Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) systems, such as topic boards, talking mats, high‑tech devices, sign and the Picture Exchange Communication System (PECS) are all complementary methods that are integrated into pupils’ programmes.
We work closely with parents and carers, celebrating progress together and facing challenges as a team. Our pupils flourish not only because of our specialist teaching and therapeutic support, but because they are surrounded by adults who believe in them wholeheartedly.
I have worked at Step by Step School for two decades and it is a privilege to lead a community where every child is known, valued, and supported to grow in confidence, independence, and joy. I believe that with the right environment, the right expertise, and the right relationships, every young person can thrive.
Whether you are exploring our school for the first time or are already part of our community, I hope this website gives you a meaningful insight into life at Step by Step. If you would like to learn more or arrange a visit, we would be delighted to welcome you.
School history
In 2000 a small group of parents with autistic children, in and around the Crowborough area, were put in touch with each other through a common interest of wanting to create a learning environment for their children.
About autism
Autism is a lifelong developmental disability. It is the result of a neurological condition which affects how the brain processes information – in particular, it can affect communication and social interaction.
5 priority learning areas
As part of our curriculum we focus on 5 key areas of learning. The school uses a range of measure to assess the progress of the pupils in these areas. For more information on our priority learning areas, you can click on any of the active links. We change our feature presentation each term.
Safeguarding
Step by Step School is committed to share this commitment.
You can view and download our Child Protection & Safeguarding Policy and Procedure as well as reading more about Safeguarding at Step by Step school here.

Our mission is:To maximise the potential of pupils with Autistic Spectrum Conditions (ASC) through evidence based, individually tailored, outstanding teaching to thrive and live happy, confident lives.

Outstanding
We’re thrilled to announce that our school has received an Outstanding Ofsted Report! This achievement reflects the incredible dedication, passion, and teamwork of our amazing staff.
New Headteacher
The governors are delighted to announce that, following a comprehensive search, Dr Olivia Kurzeja has been appointed as Headteacher with immediate effect.
Change of Leadership
Following the departure of Alastair Burnett, Olivia Kurzeja and Clare Eastwood will be taking on the roles of Interim Co-Headteachers with immediate effect.

Careers
Our Vision
Step by Step School aims to provide a pupil-centred and highly personalised careers programme that is exciting and meaningful for individual learners. Our programme is flexible and tailored to meet the specific needs of each student, equipping them with the skills required to pursue their chosen career pathway.
Our Commitment
We believe that all young people have the right to equal opportunities in their communities and workplaces. We actively promote equality and support pupils in developing the skills, understanding, and confidence to reach their full potential.
Our Approach
Recognising the unique needs of our students, we ensure that careers information and guidance are delivered by familiar and trusted staff members. From Year 8, each student develops a Vocational Profile—a living document that captures their experiences, reflections, and aspirations. This collaborative approach ensures that students are actively involved in shaping their future.
Careers Programme
Our careers programme delivers professional Careers Education, Information, Advice, and Guidance (CEIAG) through a personalised approach. Overseen by the Work Experience Co-ordinator and Curriculum Team, CEIAG is embedded into each student’s individualised learning plan. The focus is on building employability skills and, where possible, developing a clear career pathway.

Maths
Maths & Numeracy
At Step by Step School, the teaching of numeracy skills provides pupils with a foundation for their learning and supports them to develop independent living skills such as, telling the time and understanding and using money. Numeracy is an important area of learning and can lead to the development of more complex skills such as logical thinking and reasoning.
Maths and numeracy is embedded throughout pupils’ individualised programmes as well as taught during small group sessions, where these skills are taught in motivating and functional ways. For example, pupils have a range of opportunities to develop their numeracy skills when out in the community (e.g., paying for food in the supermarket and measuring wood to saw at woodwork) or measuring out ingredients when cooking lunch at school.
All numeracy targets are individualised according to each pupil’s level of understanding and their needs, preparing them for life beyond Step by Step. For some pupils, this may include working towards AQA Maths Unit Awards and Entry Level Maths.

Teaching and LEarning
Priority Learning Areas
5 Priority Learning Areas
We aim to ensure that the learning experience at Step by Step School is positive, exciting and meaningful for each individual learner with a focus on our priority learning areas:
1. Communication
2. Social Skills
3. Behaviour Attitudes
4. Community Participation
5. Independent/ Daily Living Skills
1. Communication
For Step by Step School, communication is one of the most important skills for our pupils to develop. Communication is central to psychological, social and emotional wellbeing, and academic progress. Pupils at Step by Step School have a range of needs. Therefore, it is essential that each pupil is seen as an individual who has communication methods tailored to their needs.
The school’s role is to support pupils to engage in the understanding (receptive) and use of (expressive) language and social communication. At Step by Step School this is achieved by providing a communication supportive environment using a Total Communication approach.For more information please see here.
2. Social Skills
Autistic pupils typically experience differences around social communication, interaction, and imagination. Every individual will have the opportunity to work on a variety of social skills including; sharing imaginative play, interpreting gestures/body language and many other essential skills.
Social skills play a fundamental role in our interactions with the world. It is important for pupils to develop their confidence in using these skills so that they can thrive both in and out of school, and as they transition into adulthood.
3. Behaviour and Attitudes
Behaviours of concern are well understood by staff and strategies for supporting pupils when necessary form part of the school’s curriculum.
Step by Step School’s approach to teaching and understanding behaviour is based on the principles of Applied Behaviour Analysis (ABA). Behaviour analysis recognises that all behaviour serves a function for the individual and identifying this helps us to effectively support our pupils. Through the motivational teaching approaches used at the school, pupils develop a positive attitude to learning. Learning is always centred on the pupil’s individual motivations.
All class staff are trained in Team Teach which is a positive behaviour management strategy used at Step by Step School. The positive behaviour management strategies that Team Teach develops and promotes include personal safety, communication, diversion and verbal and non-verbal de-escalation techniques. These techniques focus on dealing with behaviours of concern, which aims to reduce the need for physical intervention. As a last resort, we also are trained in positive handling techniques to resolve conflicts in ways that are safe, and which provide opportunities for repair and reflection for everyone involved. This helps to promote positive relationships in our school.
Team Teach are certified by the BILD ACT Association of Certified Training, complying with the Restraint Reduction Network Training Standards, a requirement for NHS commissioned services.
All our staff are trained in Team Teach and the school has certified Team Teach trainers onsite, who provides initial training, ongoing refreshers to staff as well as discussions about how best to support the individuals.
For more information please click here
4. Community Participation
At Step by Step School, we believe that our pupils have a right to access and become part of the local community. Community participation is embedded throughout our curriculum and pupils access regular weekly trips such as trampolining, swimming and local parks. As pupils progress through the school and start to gain confidence when out in the community, they start to use local facilities such as National Trust properties, local supermarkets and coffee shops. Once pupils have moved into years 10, 11 and into the sixth form provision, some will access work experience opportunities such as woodwork and working on a local farm.
5. Independent/Daily Living Skills
Step by Step School recognises the importance of teaching independent skills for all our pupils, at a level that is appropriate for their age and ability.
By teaching daily living skills, we help to prepare pupils for life beyond Step by Step School. Areas of focus include teaching personal care, cooking, dressing and household responsibilities.

Reading at Step by Step School
The importance of reading…
However, at Step by Step School, we understand that the journey towards becoming a reader can be a difficult one and it is for this reason that:
We strive to make reading, the love of books and stories accessible to all.
It is valued, promoted and actively encouraged. This is done through many experiences, such as sharing the enjoyment of a book with another person, a story through sensory activities, actively engaging in learning to read or understanding that words and pictures are used to communicate.
Step by Step School do not limit this experience based on cognitive ability and all pupils are encouraged to engage with books and the wonder of storytelling, developing positive experiences of reading through their educational journey with us.
It can stimulate your imagination.
Most importantly, reading is FUN!

Curriculum
Step by Step provides high quality, specialised teaching for autistic children.
Step by Step believes that:
Our Curriculum
Our curriculum provision is pupil-centred and highly personalised. We aim to ensure that the learning experience at Step by Step is positive, exciting and meaningful for each individual learner.
Our specialised curricula focuses on a wide range of developmental areas, in addition to differentiated aspects of the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) and National Curriculum, as well as AQA (Assessment and Qualifications Alliance) courses.
Step by Step School have designed a functional curriculum that meets the needs of all of our pupils, and can be tailored to suit individual strengths and abilities. The skills we teach are relevant, accessible, functional and motivating.
Teaching through the key stages
Our curriculum is taught through a combination of individual, paired and small group teaching and accommodates the learning styles and communication systems of all pupils.
To enhance the delivery of the curriculum and promote a positive learning environment we use a range of visual aids, sign language (Signalong) and reinforcement (reward) systems to appropriately support the learners.
As students’ progress through the school, the daily timetable places greater emphasis on activities that support them for adulthood. This includes community access and integration, independence, self-care, daily living skills, and promoting healthy lifestyles. Within the secondary provision, all pupils are given opportunities to work on skills necessary to live, work, socialise and pursue hobbies and recreational activities in the community.
The overriding aim of the Post 16 provision is to provide the necessary teaching and learning opportunities for every student to make a successful transition into adult life. This includes an increased focus on vocational skills and work experience.
School Enrichment and Spiritual, moral, social and cultural development (SMSC)
School enrichment opportunities cover a large part of our curriculum (such as World Book day, Discoverability, music assemblies and topic related outings) and are enjoyed across all phases of the school. Additionally, we include a variety of SMSC events throughout the academic year including onsite fire service, doctors, celebrations around the world, and history week to name a few.
All pupils take part in a wide range of weekly onsite and/or offsite PE lessons. We offer a broad range of activities for example: Basketball, Circuits, Dance, Gymnastics, Yoga, Nature exploration, Tennis, Cricket, Team games, and Athletics run by an in-house PE teacher.
Curriculum Summary
Through our Curriculum, we aim to maximise the potential of pupils with Autistic Spectrum Conditions (ASC) through evidence based, individually tailored, outstanding teaching to enable them to thrive and live happy, confident lives.

Neurodiversity
What is neurodiversity?
Neurodiversity is the concept that all human brains work differently to each other. The majority of the population are ‘neurotypical’, meaning they experience and understand the world in a way that is considered typical. Some people are considered ‘neurodivergent’, which means that they process, experience and react to the world differently to ‘neurotypical people’. Examples of conditions someone may have that are considered ‘neurodivergent’ include autism, ADHD, Tourette’s syndrome, and learning difficulties – amongst others.
What is neuro-affirming support?
Neuro-affirming support refers to any form of care that incorporates the values of the neurodiversity paradigm. These principles include the fact that all people should be valued and respected, and no brain is more ‘normal’ or ‘ideal’ than the other. Neuro-affirming support aims to identify and address barriers in the environment that people across the neurodiversity spectrum may face. Neuro-affirming support also identifies the strengths of each individual and supports them to pursue their own goals, promotes their independence and prioritises their autonomy.
Please see information from the National Autistic Society for more information: Autism and neurodiversity
Neuro-affirming practice at Step by Step
At Step by Step, we recognise that all our pupils are neurodivergent and therefore neuro-affirming practice is best practice when supporting our pupils. Staff have been accessing external training on neuro-affirming practice, and continually conduct internal reflections on the latest research and best practice, updating our terminology and strategies used across the school accordingly.
We recognise the importance of a multi-disciplinary approach, with collaboration between Behaviour Analysts, Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapists, SEND teachers, families and pupils. This approach supports the implementation of compassionate, assent-based Applied Behaviour Analysis with a focus on supporting and empowering pupils through co-regulation, self-regulation, and a total communication approach.

What is PSHE in schools?
PSHE stands for Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education.
As a subject, PSHE aims to provide children with the knowledge and skills to keep themselves happy, healthy and safe, as well as to prepare them for life and work. PSHE aims to give children the knowledge, skills and understanding they need to lead lives which are as confident, healthy and autonomous as possible.

At Step by Step School our curriculum is based upon the PSHE Association SEND Curriculum and taught by our teachers during weekly group lessons. These weekly lessons continue throughout all key stages whilst Relationship, Sex and Health Education is introduced from year 7. RSE as a subject teaches children and young adults about the different physical, social and emotional aspects of growing up, relationships and sexuality. It also helps them to develop resilience, autonomy and self-esteem. Through RSE, children can learn to better understand their own needs, respect the needs of others, and improve their overall confidence.
RSE covers important subjects such as puberty and aims to support each child and young adult through their individual challenges. These private areas of need are discussed with parents and carers, planned and taught in a 1:1 setting.
Parents are offered information workshops around this subject at the start of each academic year and are always welcome to discuss any questions they may have with the PSHE lead.

School History
The history of Step by Step School
Step By Step school was founded in 2000 by a group of parents as an Independent day school for autism. We opened our doors to our first pupils in 2004. We have been teaching children ever since and are proud to say we’ve been able to assist over 90 pupils and families, using our holistic education, based on the principles of Applied Behavioural Analysis. The school has grown considerably in pupil numbers, currently having a capacity for 40. We have invested significantly in our buildings, resources and surroundings to provide an excellent learning environment for our pupils.
The school is very proud of its humble beginnings and recognises this could not have been possible without a huge effort over the years from all our supporters and community groups. We celebrated our 20th anniversary in 2024 where we were delighted to welcome back past pupils, families, staff, governors, fund-raisers and others from our local community.
We are looking forward to our next 20 years!

About autism
What is Autism?
Autism, also known as Autism Spectrum Condition (ASC) or Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) presents differently for everyone. However, there are some characteristics that are shared by autistic people.
Autistic people may:
Autism is a spectrum and therefore all autistic people have these characteristics to differing degrees, and require different levels of support.
Autism is a developmental condition, which means that it is something that people are born with, although the signs may be noticed at any age.
Autistic people can have any level of intelligence, some people have above average intelligence and some autistic people may also have a learning disability.
Autism does not have a known cause, but there is some evidence to suggest it can be passed on through families. It is not caused by bad parenting, vaccines, diet or infection (NHS, 2022).
Autistic people often have other conditions, including ADHD, dyslexia, anxiety, depression and epilepsy (NHS, 2022).
